patients.summary: Retired postal worker with ESRD from hypertensive nephrosclerosis, a failed 2016 kidney graft and a December 2020 re-transplant, and bipolar I disorder on lithium. His transplant course brings lithium nephrogenic DI, tacrolimus toxicity, acute and later chronic rejection, and three opportunistic infections (Pneumocystis, nocardiosis, cryptococcal meningitis).

Records packet from patient's previous primary care office, 41 pages, covering 2012 to 2019.

Highlights pulled by MA for PCP review:
- Hypertension for many years; kidney failure attributed to hypertensive nephrosclerosis, hemodialysis, then deceased-donor kidney transplant 2016.
- 2017: rejection episode treated by the transplant center with high-dose cyclophosphamide; complicated by hemorrhagic cystitis (gross hematuria, suprapubic pain), managed with IV hydration and mesna; finished the drug without further bladder trouble.
- 2019: transplant note copy, graft failed, back on in-center hemodialysis since March.
- Bipolar disorder type I on lithium since 2011, managed by his psychiatrist.
- Screening colonoscopy 2017 for transplant listing: normal to the terminal ileum, no polyps, 10-year interval.
- Hepatitis C antibody and HIV screen negative 2017 (listing labs).
- Tdap 2017.
- No known drug allergies.

Filed to chart.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
54 y/o man transferring primary care. Non-dialysis day. Sharp historian, has a typed medication list.

Kidneys: long-standing HTN -> ESRD (hypertensive nephrosclerosis), HD, then deceased-donor transplant 2016. Several rejections with that graft; the 2017 one needed high-dose cyclophosphamide and he developed hemorrhagic cystitis, treated with hydration and mesna, no bladder problems since. Graft failed early this year and he is back on in-center HD M/W/F through a L forearm fistula. Relisted at the transplant center. Transplant kept him on prednisone 5 mg; tacrolimus and mycophenolate were stopped when the graft failed.

Psych: bipolar I, on lithium since 2011, no admissions in years. His psychiatrist adjusted lithium for dialysis: one 300 mg capsule after each run, levels drawn at the unit.

Other: HTN on amlodipine. Former smoker, quit 2016. No alcohol. Retired from the postal service. Married. Fishes most mornings he is not at dialysis; used to fish bass tournaments when younger.

Family: father HTN and CKD. Sister bipolar disorder. Maternal uncle ESRD.

Meds: prednisone 5 daily, lithium 300 mg after HD, amlodipine 10 daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 138/86. Well appearing. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed RLQ transplant incision, nontender. L forearm AV fistula with good thrill. No edema. Neuro nonfocal. Mood euthymic, linear.

PHQ-9: 3.

A/P
1. ESRD on HD, failed 2016 graft, relisted: dialysis unit draws monthly labs; asked them to copy us. Transplant center remains lead for immunosuppression.
2. HTN: acceptable on amlodipine for a dialysis patient, unit tracks pre/post pressures.
3. Bipolar I, stable: lithium per psychiatry. Will request his psychiatrist's notes.
4. Hx cyclophosphamide hemorrhagic cystitis, resolved.
5. Health maintenance: colonoscopy 2017 normal (due 2027). Tdap 2017. Flu shot next month; no live vaccines.
RTC 3 months.

Patient: Ousmane Diallo. Modality: in-center hemodialysis three times weekly, 4 hours. Access: left forearm AV fistula, functioning well, no interventions this quarter.
Adequacy at goal. Interdialytic weight gains modest. Pre-dialysis BP generally 130s-140s systolic on amlodipine.
Monthly labs reviewed with the patient and acceptable for dialysis; no changes to his dialysis prescription.
Active on the deceased-donor transplant wait list.
Allergies: NKDA.
Copy to primary care per patient request.

Mr. Diallo has bipolar I disorder, euthymic for many years on lithium. Since resuming hemodialysis he takes lithium carbonate 300 mg after each session; the dialysis unit draws a pre-dialysis level every month and his levels have stayed in the range we want. No mood episodes, sleeping well, no psychotic symptoms. Wife reports no concerns.

Plan: continue same dosing; when he receives a kidney he should call us so we can return him to twice-daily dosing with closer levels.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Transplant center discharge summary
documents.author: transplant surgery
documents.body:
Academic transplant center, inpatient transplant surgery service.
Admitted 12/03/2020. Discharged 12/10/2020.

Procedure: deceased-donor kidney transplant (second graft), 12/03/2020. First graft (2016) left in situ.
Indication: ESRD from hypertensive nephrosclerosis; failure of first graft after rejection episodes, on hemodialysis since 03/2019.

Course: immediate graft function, no dialysis needed after surgery. Creatinine fell steadily, 1.4 on the morning of discharge. Steroid taper started; prednisone to return to 5 mg daily per the taper calendar given to the patient. Psychiatry consulted for lithium now that he has a working kidney: back to 300 mg twice daily with a level in one week.

Discharge medications:
- tacrolimus 5 mg twice daily (levels at clinic)
- mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg twice daily
- prednisone per taper, then 5 mg daily
- trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole single strength daily (Pneumocystis prophylaxis)
- valganciclovir 450 mg daily for 6 months (CMV prophylaxis)
- lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily
- amlodipine 10 mg daily

Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: transplant clinic twice weekly for the first month. Hemodialysis discontinued; dialysis unit notified.

documents.title: Video Visit: After Kidney Transplant
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, patient at home, wife present. Got his second kidney 12/3, home 12/10. Making plenty of urine, says it is strange not going to dialysis. Incision healing, a little sore. No fever. Transplant clinic twice a week, labs good so far per patient.

Med reconciliation from the discharge summary: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone taper down to 5 mg, TMP-SMX SS daily, valganciclovir 450 daily x 6 months, lithium back to 300 mg BID (psychiatry following the level), amlodipine 10 daily. Our list updated.

A/P: s/p deceased-donor re-transplant, early course smooth. Transplant team manages immunosuppression and labs. Talked about avoiding NSAIDs and checking with us/transplant before any new medicine. Will see in person in a few months; COVID vaccine as soon as he is eligible.

documents.author: transplant nephrology
documents.body:
Transplant nephrology clinic, 10-week post-transplant visit.

Dear colleague,
Mr. Diallo is doing well ten weeks after his second deceased-donor kidney. Creatinine today 1.2, his new baseline. Prednisone is down to 5 mg daily. Tacrolimus trough in target on 5 mg twice daily.
His clinic pressures have run in the 140s/90s on amlodipine 10 mg, now that he is off dialysis and making urine. We added hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily today.

Current medications: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, TMP-SMX SS daily, valganciclovir 450 mg daily (through early June), lithium 300 mg BID per psychiatry, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Next visit in 6 weeks.
Transplant nephrology

We will check a level with each of his transplant draws every few months and see him twice a year.

Meds reviewed: tacrolimus 5 BID, mycophenolate 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS daily, valganciclovir 450 daily until June, lithium 300 BID, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25 (added by transplant in Feb).

Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear. Graft in R iliac fossa nontender, incision healed. No edema. No tremor.

1. s/p re-transplant 12/2020: stable per transplant.
2. HTN: better with HCTZ added.
3. Bipolar I: stable, lithium per psychiatry; TSH today.
4. On prednisone and tacrolimus: lipids and A1c today.
5. Prevention: pneumococcal and shingles vaccines to plan once further out from transplant, per transplant timing.
RTC 4-6 months.

documents.title: Transplant medicine clinic letter
documents.author: transplant medicine
documents.body:
Transplant medicine clinic. Date of visit: 06/04/2021.

Routine follow-up, six months after his second deceased-donor kidney (12/2020; first graft 2016). His first graft had several rejection episodes; one was treated with high-dose cyclophosphamide, complicated by hemorrhagic cystitis that settled with vigorous hydration and mesna, and he completed that treatment with no return of bladder symptoms.

He is taking his immunosuppression and prophylactic antibiotic reliably, even with his long mornings out fishing. No blood in the urine, no burning or frequency. No fevers, chills or sweats. Otherwise a negative review.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 76, RR 14.
Exam: well, comfortable. Normal heart and lung exam. Abdomen with healed incision, no tenderness, no organomegaly. No peripheral edema. Neurologically nonfocal.

Labs today: creatinine 1.2, electrolytes normal, CBC normal, urinalysis normal.

Plan: six months of valganciclovir completed, stop today. Continue tacrolimus 5 mg BID (trough in target), mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, TMP-SMX SS daily. Amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25 and lithium unchanged.
Allergies: NKDA. Return in 3 months.

documents.title: Office Visit: Thirst and Urination
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About a week of being thirsty all the time and peeing a lot, up 3-4 times a night. Carrying a jug of water in the truck. No burning, no blood, no fever. No new meds. Graft site not tender.
Meds: tacrolimus 5 BID, mycophenolate 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS, lithium 300 BID (since 2011), amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25.

O: Vitals as charted, afebrile. Mucous membranes moist. Graft nontender. No edema. No tremor.
UA in office: no glucose, no protein, no blood.

A/P: polyuria/polydipsia in a man on long-term lithium with a 9-month-old graft. Not diabetic glucose-wise. Concern for lithium effect on urine concentrating. BMP today. Referring to nephrology (transplant aware, agreeable). Keep drinking to thirst, do not restrict water.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood sugar was normal, so this is not diabetes. Kidney function is steady. Nephrology will call you to schedule; the referral went in yesterday.

documents.title: Nephrology consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient nephrology. Date of service: 08/23/2021. Referred by primary care.

Reason: two weeks of heavy urination and thirst.

HPI: Kidney recipient (second graft 12/2020) seen at transplant clinic in June. Now drinking upward of 4 liters a day and still feels parched. Has taken lithium for bipolar I for about ten years, with excellent mood control; also on hydrochlorothiazide for blood pressure.

PMH: ESRD from hypertensive nephrosclerosis; transplants 2016 and 2020; HTN; bipolar I.
Meds: tacrolimus, mycophenolate, prednisone 5 mg, TMP-SMX SS, lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father HTN and CKD; sister bipolar disorder; maternal uncle ESRD.
Social: former smoker, quit 5 years ago. No alcohol. Retired from the post office.

Vitals within normal limits. Exam without abnormality.

Data:
- Serum sodium 145 mEq/L
- Serum osmolality 300 mOsm/kg
- Urine osmolality 150 mOsm/kg
- Urine specific gravity 1.005
- Desmopressin given in clinic; urine osmolality 160 mOsm/kg two hours later

Impression: dilute urine with a high-normal sodium and raised serum osmolality, no meaningful response to desmopressin. Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, most consistent with long-term lithium.

Recommendations: unrestricted access to water at all times; discussed with his psychiatrist, who prefers to keep lithium given a decade of stability, and we agree to continue it for now. Continue hydrochlorothiazide. Sodium with his transplant labs. Happy to see him again as needed.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: COVID-19 Additional Dose
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Third primary dose of Moderna for an immunocompromised patient (transplant recipient), IM L deltoid. Observed 15 min, no issue. Nephrology note from 8/23 is in the chart; he is drinking freely as advised.

documents.title: Transplant medicine clinic letter
documents.author: transplant medicine
documents.body:
Transplant medicine clinic. Date of visit: 12/08/2021.

56-year-old recipient of a second deceased-donor kidney (12/2020). Two weeks of shaky hands, plus more thirst and urination again, much like the stretch that took him to nephrology in August.

Meds: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, TMP-SMX SS daily, lithium 300 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.

BP 150/95. Fine tremor of both outstretched hands. Otherwise unremarkable.

Labs (fasting): creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (high; baseline 1.2), BUN 35, glucose 160, tacrolimus trough 15 ng/mL (inside the lab's reported range but well above where we keep him now), lithium 0.8 mmol/L.

Assessment: calcineurin inhibitor nephrotoxicity, with tacrolimus tremor and hyperglycemia. Lithium level unremarkable.

Plan: tacrolimus reduced to 3 mg twice daily starting tonight. Repeat trough and creatinine in 1 week and again in 4 weeks. Primary care please recheck glucose/A1c once the dose settles.
Transplant medicine

documents.title: Tacrolimus change
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Transplant cut my tacrolimus to 3 pills twice a day because my kidney number went up and my hands are shaking. Do I need to do anything with you? Also is my sugar a problem now?

documents.title: RE: Tacrolimus change
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got their letter. The lower dose should take care of the shaking and the kidney number, and the higher sugar was most likely from the tacrolimus level. Keep your January visit; we'll check an A1c then.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Hand shaking gone within about ten days of the tacrolimus cut to 3 mg BID. Still thirstier than he used to be, keeps water close, nocturia twice. Transplant rechecked the trough twice and is happy with it.
Meds: tacrolimus 3 BID, mycophenolate 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS, lithium 300 BID, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25.

O: Vitals as charted. No tremor. Heart, lungs normal. Graft nontender. No edema.
BMP and A1c drawn here today; A1c 5.5, creatinine back to 1.2.

A/P
1. Tacrolimus toxicity: resolved on the lower dose, kidney function back to baseline. The December glucose of 160 was the tacrolimus; A1c normal, no diabetes.
2. Nephrogenic DI on lithium: per nephrology, free water.
3. HTN: reasonable today.
4. Vaccines: PCV20 and first Shingrix today (non-live, fine with his transplant). Second Shingrix in 2-6 months.
RTC 3 months.

documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outside psychiatry practice, semiannual review.
Bipolar I, euthymic. Aware of the nephrology diagnosis of lithium-related nephrogenic DI; after reviewing the alternatives with him and his wife, he wants to stay on lithium, which has kept him well for over a decade. Tremor from December resolved with the transplant team's tacrolimus change; his lithium level then was 0.8.
Continue lithium carbonate 300 mg BID. Levels with transplant labs. Return in 6 months.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Office Visit: Blood Pressure
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: His home cuff has been creeping up since around the new year, now mostly 150s/90s. Taking amlodipine and HCTZ every day, wife confirms. Thinks he is passing a bit less urine than he was. No headache, chest pain, fever or graft pain. No NSAIDs.

O: BP 154/94 (repeat similar). Vitals otherwise as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear, graft nontender, no edema.
BMP today: creatinine 1.6, up from 1.2 in January.

A/P: rising pressure and creatinine in a 15-month-old graft on tacrolimus 3 BID. Needs the transplant team this week or next, not in June. Not adding a third BP drug before they see him. Messaged transplant clinic with today's numbers. Patient knows to go to the ED for fever, graft pain, or a sharp drop in urine.

documents.title: Transplant medicine clinic letter
documents.author: transplant medicine
documents.body:
Transplant medicine clinic. Date of visit: 04/21/2022. Seen early at primary care's request.

56-year-old with a second deceased-donor kidney (12/2020), calcineurin inhibitor toxicity in December, and lithium nephrogenic DI from August. Three months of climbing blood pressure though he takes hydrochlorothiazide and amlodipine faithfully. Less urine lately. Creatinine has gone from 1.2 to 1.9 over the past two months.

Meds: tacrolimus 3 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg, TMP-SMX SS, lithium 300 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg. Allergies: NKDA.

BP 162/98.
Exam: grade 3/6 systolic bruit, loudest over the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. Rest of the exam unremarkable.

Labs: creatinine 1.9 (baseline 1.2), BUN 36, potassium 4.8, hemoglobin 13.2. Urinalysis: no protein, no blood.

Assessment: graft dysfunction with worsening hypertension; acute rejection of the kidney is the main concern.
Plan: percutaneous allograft biopsy scheduled for 04/26. Hold further antihypertensive changes until the biopsy result is back.

conditions.label: Kidney transplant rejection
conditions.note: acute T-cell-mediated rejection, Banff IA, second graft

medications.sig: 500 mg IV daily for 3 days (04/27-04/29/2022)

reports.text:
Specimen: transplant kidney, percutaneous needle core biopsy x2.
Adequacy: adequate, 14 glomeruli, 2 arteries.
Light microscopy: interstitial mononuclear inflammation involving more than 25% of the unscarred cortex with moderate tubulitis. Glomeruli unremarkable. Arteries without intimal arteritis. No significant interstitial fibrosis or tubular atrophy.
Immunofluorescence: C4d negative in peritubular capillaries.
Electron microscopy: pending, to follow if contributory.
reports.conclusion: Acute T-cell-mediated rejection, Banff grade IA.

documents.title: Transplant medicine letter: biopsy and treatment
documents.author: transplant medicine
documents.body:
Transplant medicine.
Allograft biopsy 04/26/2022: acute T-cell-mediated rejection, Banff IA, C4d negative.
Treated in our infusion unit with methylprednisolone 500 mg IV daily on 04/27, 04/28 and 04/29, then back to prednisone 5 mg daily. No change to tacrolimus 3 mg BID or mycophenolate 750 mg BID; trough in target.
Creatinine checks weekly for a month. We discussed adherence and he reports no missed doses.
Will update primary care with follow-up labs.

Initial Medicare wellness visit (Medicare through ESRD).

Interval: April allograft biopsy showed acute cellular rejection, treated with three days of IV methylprednisolone by transplant. Creatinine 1.4 in May, 1.2 today: back to baseline. Feels well. Fishing most mornings again. Thirst persists, manageable.

Meds: tacrolimus 3 BID, mycophenolate 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS, lithium 300 BID, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25. NKDA.

PHQ-9 2. AUDIT-C 0. Former smoker, quit 2016.

Exam: BP 132/82. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, graft nontender, no bruit appreciated today. Skin without lesions of concern. No edema. Mood euthymic.

Prevention: colonoscopy 2017 normal, due 2027. Hep C/HIV screened 2017. PCV20 done. Shingrix #2 today. Tdap 2017. COVID 3 doses; flu each fall. Yearly skin check with dermatology advised for transplant recipients; referral offered, he will set it up through transplant's dermatology clinic.

A/P: acute rejection treated, resolved by labs. HTN controlled today. Bipolar I stable. Labs today. RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Seen 10/18/2022.

CC: dry cough, breathless on exertion, low fevers for a week.
HPI: 57-year-old man with a kidney transplant, a prior rejection episode and calcineurin inhibitor toxicity. New nonproductive cough, winded on stairs, temperatures to the high 99s for about a week. No travel, no sick contacts. Says he takes everything as prescribed, including his TMP-SMX and valganciclovir.
Meds per list: tacrolimus, mycophenolate, prednisone, TMP-SMX, valganciclovir, lithium, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: T 37.8 C, BP 135/85, HR 88, RR 20, SpO2 94% room air.
Exam: crackles at both bases. No distress at rest.

Results: WBC 6,500, Hgb 12.5, plt 250,000. Creatinine 1.2, BUN 21. LDH 220 (high). ABG on room air: pH 7.45, PaCO2 35, PaO2 72.
CXR: diffuse interstitial infiltrates.

Impression: suspected Pneumocystis pneumonia in an immunosuppressed host. Admitted to medicine, induced sputum sent.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary

Regional hospital, medicine service. Admitted 10/18/2022, discharged 10/24/2022.

Diagnosis: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (induced sputum PCR positive 10/19).
Course: started on treatment-dose trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, two double-strength tablets three times daily, on admission; daily prophylactic dose held. PaO2 above 70 on room air, so no adjunctive steroids. Oxygen never needed beyond 2 L for walking on day 1. Fever resolved day 3. Creatinine and potassium followed daily with transplant input and stayed stable; tacrolimus continued.
Discharge medications: TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs TID to complete 21 days (last dose 11/07/2022), then resume single strength daily. Tacrolimus 3 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, lithium 300 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week; transplant clinic 2 weeks; BMP in 5 days.

2. Transplant: they see him in 2 weeks.
Portal or call if fever or worse breathing.

Regional hospital emergency department. Date of visit 04/17/2023.

CC: ten days of cough that keeps getting worse, fevers, losing weight.
HPI: 57-year-old kidney transplant recipient with Pneumocystis pneumonia last fall. Besides the cough he has had a dull headache for about a week and some trouble keeping his focus. No recent travel or sick contacts. Taking his immunosuppression as prescribed, tacrolimus and prednisone included.
Meds: tacrolimus 3 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg, TMP-SMX SS daily, lithium 300 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father hypertension and CKD; sister bipolar disorder; maternal uncle ESRD.
Social: does not smoke (quit years ago); no recent travel or known sick contacts.

Vitals: T 38.4 C (101.1 F), RR 22, HR 96, BP 128/80, SpO2 95% RA.
Exam: crackles over the right upper lobe. Neuro exam nonfocal.

Sputum Gram stain: branching gram-positive rods, Nocardia.
CXR: cavitary right upper lobe lesion.
MRI brain: single ring-enhancing lesion, frontal lobe.

Impression: nocardiosis involving lung and brain. Admitted; ID and transplant consulted.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, medicine service. Admitted 04/17/2023, discharged 05/01/2023.

Diagnosis: nocardiosis, pulmonary and central nervous system.
Course: IV trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (high dose, renally adjusted) and IV imipenem started on admission. Sputum culture final 04/24: Nocardia species. Neurosurgery reviewed the MRI; with a sputum diagnosis and a small single lesion, medical treatment with serial imaging was chosen, no aspiration. Headache resolved by day 5, fevers by day 4. Creatinine and potassium watched daily, stable. Transplant continued tacrolimus 3 mg BID and mycophenolate.
After 2 weeks of IV therapy transitioned to oral TMP-SMX DS 2 tablets twice daily, planned for 12 months total given brain involvement; this replaces his daily prophylactic tablet.
Discharge medications: TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs BID; tacrolimus 3 mg BID; mycophenolate 750 mg BID; prednisone 5 mg daily; lithium 300 mg BID; amlodipine 10 mg; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: infectious disease 6 weeks with repeat brain MRI; primary care 1 week; weekly BMP and CBC for a month.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharged 5/1 after two weeks for nocardia in the lung and a small brain lesion.
S: Headache gone, thinking clear, wife agrees he is himself. Cough mostly gone. Appetite coming back; down to 81 kg from 86. No fever. Taking TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs twice a day, plenty of water.
O: Weight 81 kg. Vitals as charted, afebrile. Lungs: faint crackles R upper field. Neuro: alert, oriented, fluent, strength and gait normal.
Records reviewed and med list reconciled (SS prophylaxis replaced by the treatment course).
A/P
1. Nocardiosis, lung and brain: 12-month oral course, ID follow-up with MRI in June/July. Weekly BMP/CBC; drawn today.
2. Weight loss from the illness: high-calorie foods, recheck weight next visit.
3. Driving: hold until ID/neurosurgery say otherwise; he agreed, wife is driving.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: A whole year?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Is it right that I need to take these big antibiotic pills for a whole year? That seems like a lot. I feel fine now.

documents.title: RE: A whole year?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, that is the standard length when nocardia has reached the brain, especially with a transplant, because it can come back if stopped early. Infectious disease will follow your MRI and decide the stop date. Keep your labs going so we can watch your kidney and potassium on the higher dose.

reports.conclusion: Interval decrease of the frontal lobe lesion.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (ICU and medicine)
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted via the emergency department to the medical ICU 10/15/2023; transferred to medicine 10/19; discharged 10/31/2023.

Presentation: 58-year-old kidney recipient, history of Pneumocystis pneumonia (2022) and nocardiosis of lung and brain (04/2023, on oral TMP-SMX), brought in by his wife after one day of fever and neck pain. Temperature 103 F (39.4 C) on arrival, HR 108. Neck stiff and painful to flex.
Meds on admission: tacrolimus 3 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg, TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs BID, lithium 300 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father hypertension and CKD; sister bipolar disorder; maternal uncle ESRD.
Social: former smoker, quit about 7 years ago; no alcohol; retired postal worker.

Workup: lumbar puncture with opening pressure 31 cm H2O. CSF cryptococcal antigen positive, titer 1:640; CSF fungal culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans. Serum cryptococcal antigen positive.

Diagnosis: cryptococcal meningitis.
Course: induction with liposomal amphotericin B and flucytosine for 14 days (completed 10/28), with daily creatinine and electrolytes; IV fluids with each amphotericin dose. Two further therapeutic lumbar punctures on days 2 and 4 for raised pressure; headache and neck pain settled. Fever resolved by day 5. ICU for the first four days for neuro checks, never intubated. Transplant service lowered tacrolimus to 2 mg BID ahead of fluconazole.

Discharge medications: fluconazole 400 mg daily for 8 weeks (consolidation), then ID to set maintenance; tacrolimus 2 mg BID; mycophenolate 750 mg BID; prednisone 5 mg daily; TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs BID (nocardia course continues); lithium 300 mg BID; amlodipine 10 mg; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Follow-up: ID 4-6 weeks, transplant 1 week with tacrolimus level, primary care 1 week.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Home since 10/31 after cryptococcal meningitis: ICU 4 days, two weeks of amphotericin and flucytosine.
S: Tired but improving daily. No headache, neck pain gone, no fever. Wife giving him his pill box. Taking fluconazole 400 daily, tacrolimus now 2 mg BID (transplant drew a level yesterday), TMP-SMX DS 2 BID, rest unchanged.
O: Vitals as charted, afebrile. Alert, oriented, conversation normal. Neck supple. Gait steady. No edema.
Discharge summary reviewed, list reconciled (tacrolimus 2 BID, fluconazole added).
A/P
1. Cryptococcal meningitis, after induction: fluconazole consolidation 8 wk; ID follow-up booked.
2. Nocardiosis: continues oral course.
3. Electrolytes after amphotericin: BMP and magnesium today.
4. Third opportunistic infection in a year; asked transplant whether his overall immunosuppression should be revisited, they will review.
RTC 3 months, sooner as needed.

Transplant medicine clinic. Date of visit: 06/15/2026.

61-year-old with ESRD from hypertensive nephrosclerosis, second deceased-donor kidney 12/2020, and prior calcineurin inhibitor nephrotoxicity, here for follow-up. Over about eight months he has become steadily more tired, can do less before he has to stop, and his ankles swell by evening. His pressures have been harder to hold despite his current antihypertensives. He acknowledges missing doses now and then. Denies fever, dysuria, hematuria and abdominal pain.

Meds: tacrolimus 3 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, TMP-SMX SS daily, lithium 300 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father hypertension and CKD; sister bipolar disorder; maternal uncle ESRD.

BP 158/96. Ankle edema on both sides.

Labs: creatinine 2.6, rising gradually over the past year; urine protein/creatinine 0.6 (mild proteinuria).
Allograft ultrasound 05/28: asymmetrically small kidney, corticomedullary differentiation lost.
Allograft biopsy 06/04: fibrous intimal thickening of vessels with mononuclear infiltrates and interstitial fibrosis.

Assessment: chronic rejection of the kidney allograft. Function keeps falling even with optimized immunosuppression.

Plan:
- Adherence plan with the transplant pharmacist; same tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone.
- Furosemide 40 mg daily for the swelling.
- Vascular surgery referral to plan dialysis access.
- Re-transplant evaluation started.
We will keep primary care updated.
